title: Partner marketplace messaging matrix and certification tasks
body:
Purpose and scope:
This doc collects proposed marketplace listing copy (title, short blurb, bullets), channel-specific messaging variants, and an actionable certification & acceptance checklist for partner listings (AWS/Azure/GCP marketplaces + vendor portals). It’s intended to be a single source-of-truth for the next sprint: prep assets, legal review, SKU mapping, and launch acceptance.

Status note (quick):
- Drafted after sync 2025-01-09 with product, legal, and solutions.
- Open items highlighted as TODO / QUESTION below.
- Primary owner: Maya Patel (go-to-market). Engineering validation owner: Jonah Lee. Legal/cert owner: Priya Desai.

1) Messaging matrix (canonical listing copy)
A. Canonical title (for catalog index):
- Redwood Inference — High-performance LLM inference (hosted, dedicated, private)

B. Short blurb (1–2 lines, for search & quick read):
- Production-grade LLM inference with flexible deployment modes, predictable latency SLAs, and cost controls for engineering teams. Streamline serving across hosted API, reserved capacity, and private deployments.

C. Long description (300–450 chars, marketplace detail area):
- Redwood Inference provides a unified runtime and orchestration for LLM serving optimized for latency, throughput and economics. Ship generative features faster with a single API for text generation, chat, embeddings and reranking. Choose hosted for fastest time-to-value, reserved capacity for predictable throughput and isolation, or private deployment for regulated workloads with VPC and KMS integrations.

D. Key bullets (for marketplace feature list):
- Multi-deployment support: hosted API, dedicated GPU pools, private VPC/on-prem packages
- Cost controls: batching, KV cache, quantization recommendations, token-level spend insights
- Reliability: automated fallbacks, canary rollouts, SLA-backed capacity options
- Observability: per-route latency/cost breakdowns, tracing hooks, and regression alerts
- Secure by design: KMS/HSM integrations, audit logs, SOC2-ready controls (contact Security for region specifics)

E. Use-case callouts (short snippets to increase discoverability):
- Low-latency chat assistants (consumer apps)
- Document understanding & retrieval-augmented generation for enterprise apps
- Batch embedding pipelines and semantic search
- On-prem inference for regulated financial and healthcare workloads

F. 1-sentence technical highlight for infra-minded buyers:
- GPU-optimized runtime with dynamic batching, KV-cache reuse, and quantization-aware kernels to lower per-token cost while meeting latency SLOs.

2) Channel-specific variants (copy examples to A/B test)
- AWS Marketplace title variant: Redwood Inference — Managed inference for LLMs (SLA & reserved capacity)
- Azure Marketplace short blurb variant: Fast, reliable LLM serving with private deployment and enterprise identity integrations
- GCP listing feature focus: High-throughput inference engine with cost-aware routing and autoscaling reserved pools

3) Creative assets inventory (what we need)
- 1 hero 1200x600 PNG (clear product name, short blurb)
- 3x 800x450 feature tiles (latency, cost, security)
- 2x screenshots: Console route-level dashboard + rollout page (with blurred PII)
- 1 technical diagram (runtime + routing + cache flow) SVG
- Logo: transparent PNG + monochrome SVG

4) Billing/SKU & entitlements mapping (checklist)
- Decide SKU model (initial recommendation): usage-based hosted SKU (tokens/embedding units) + reserved capacity monthly SKU packages (bronze/silver/gold)
- Map internal plan names to marketplace SKUs and labels (TODO: confirm internal plan IDs with Finance)
- Entitlements: boolean flags for private deployment add-on, extended retention, premium SLA
- Trials: confirm trial credits and trial duration (propose 14-day credits for new marketplace customers)

5) Certification & technical acceptance checklist (owner tags + due dates)
- [ ] Product listing draft approved by Product (owner: Maya, due: 2025-01-20)
- [ ] Security questionnaire completed (owner: Priya, due: 2025-01-27)
- [ ] Privacy/Data residency note for each region (owner: Priya, due: 2025-01-27)
- [ ] Legal T&Cs + marketplace addendum reviewed (owner: Legal - assigned via Jira JIRA-GTM-742, due: 2025-01-31)
- [ ] Billing SKU mapping complete in Finance portal (owner: Liam, due: 2025-01-24)
- [ ] Images and screenshots uploaded to vendor portal (owner: Jonah, due: 2025-01-22)
- [ ] Technical on-boarding workbook (step-by-step enablement doc) attached (owner: Solutions Eng, due: 2025-01-28)
- [ ] E2E installation test for private deployment package (owner: Eng-private-deploys, due: 2025-01-30)
- [ ] Acceptance test run (functional + perf smoke) in target marketplace environment (owner: SRE, due: 2025-02-02)

6) Launch acceptance criteria (measurable)
- Marketplace listing live with approved title, 3 bullets, hero asset, and long description
- Billing entitlements show up correctly in partner portal and downstream billing pipeline
- Console onboarding flow completes in <8 minutes for a hosted API trial with default sample app
- Latency smoke test: 95th percentile generation <200ms for 64-token requests on hosted tier within region
- Security: completed questionnaire with no high findings; any medium findings have mitigation plan and owner

7) Copy variations and experiments (notes for A/B)
- Test 1: Emphasize "cost-aware serving" vs "latency-first serving" headline — track click-through and trial starts per channel
- Test 2: Short description that mentions "engineer-first API" vs generic "enterprise-grade inference"
- KPI to track: trial conversion rate, time-to-first-successful-API-call, average tokens used in trial week 1

8) Known open questions / TODOs
- TODO: Confirm exact SOC/ISO wording allowed in marketplace listing (Priya -> Legal).
- QUESTION: Do we include model names or only capability descriptors? Engineering prefers capability descriptors to avoid model-specific support. Decision needed.
- TODO: Finalize trial credit amount and gateway for marketplace-captured customers (Finance + Billing).
- TODO: Validate screenshot privacy blur threshold with privacy team (Priya).

9) Quick-runbook for partner portal submission (step-by-step)
- Prepare assets folder (image names must match: hero.png, tile-1.png, tile-2.png)
- Fill copy fields in portal: title, short blurb, long desc, bullets, use cases
- Enter SKU IDs and trial entitlements
- Upload seller contact & support email (support+marketplace@redwood.ai)
- Submit security questionnaire link and attach workbook
- Flag PR with engineering for final smoke run and provide marketplace staging credentials

10) Slack & PR hooks (where to coordinate)
- Slack channel: #gtm-marketplace (use for go/no-go and last-minute asks)
- Channel owner: Maya Patel
- PRs: https://github.com/redwood-inference/marketplace-prs/pull/92 (contains draft listing JSON)

Appendix: Sample one-line customer-facing tagline options (pick one)
- "Predictable LLM inference at cloud scale."
- "Ship LLM features with predictable latency and lower per-token cost."
- "High-performance LLM serving for teams that need SLAs and control."

Notes to reviewers:
- Please suggest final hero tagline in comments. If you edit copy, leave change notes and rationales.
- If you own an acceptance item above, mark it completed in JIRA-GTM-742 and ping in #gtm-marketplace.

-- End of draft --

Footers / versioning:
- v0.3 draft (2025-02-02)
- Author: Maya Patel (go-to-market)
- Next sync: 2025-02-03 10:00 PST (tentative)
